P-ELS.summary: Authors may use AI tools in a supportive way with human oversight and must include a separate AI declaration statement in the manuscript, though basic grammar/spelling checks and accessibility tools are exempt. AI cannot be an author, and AI images are allowed only for explanatory figures and data-derived visualizations, not primary research images. Reviewers and editors may use AI only in a supportive capacity and must not upload manuscripts into AI tools.

Reviewers should not upload a submitted manuscript or any part of it into an AI tool
Editors may therefore only use AI tools in a supportive capacity, for example to improve the language or structure of their decision letters

P-WIL.summary: Wiley welcomes responsible use of AI by authors as a companion to writing, provided authors keep full accountability, review the tools' terms, protect rights, and disclose use. Disclosure is required for substantial text generation, restructuring, translation, methodology use, and visuals, but not for simple grammar, formatting, or word-choice polishing. AI-edited photographs and factual or evidential images are not permitted, AI cannot be an author, and reviewers and editors must not upload manuscripts to AI tools but may use AI for organizing and polishing their reviews, with disclosure of drafting assistance.

P-SAG.summary: Sage separates assistive AI use (language, grammar, structure), which needs no disclosure, from generative AI use that affects content, methods, results or images, which must be disclosed and verified by authors. Reviewers may use GenAI to help write and format reports but must not upload manuscripts to AI tools. Editors must not use GenAI for decision letters, summaries of unpublished research, or editorial work.

P-OUP.summary: Authors may use generative AI tools when preparing manuscripts. Basic language correction and reference formatting need no disclosure, while substantial editing, translation, data analysis, code, and illustrative images must be disclosed. Fabricating research data or creating/altering primary scientific images is not allowed, and non-disclosure may lead to rejection, correction, or retraction.

P-SPR.summary: Springer Nature uses a green/amber/red risk framework for AI across authors, reviewers and editors. Low-risk assistive uses such as language polishing are permitted, with disclosure encouraged. Interpretive uses are permitted only with human oversight, verification and disclosure. Uses that replace human judgement, are undisclosed, fabricate content, list AI as an author or delegate peer review to AI are not permitted. Reviewers must not upload manuscript content to unsecured or public AI tools.

P-EME.summary: Emerald bans using generative AI to write or generate new content, data or results, but permits AI copy-editing of the author's own work, translation, and illustrative images, with transparent declaration and human accountability. AI cannot be an author. Reviewers and editors may not use generative AI to evaluate manuscripts or upload files to AI tools, though reviewers may use it to copy-edit their review reports and must declare this.

P-TF.summary: Authors may use generative AI responsibly for tasks like idea generation, copyediting, translation, literature classification and coding help, but must verify outputs and disclose the tool, version, how and why it was used. AI cannot be an author, and AI may not be used to create or manipulate research results or diagnostic images. Editors and reviewers must never upload unpublished manuscripts into AI tools; reviewers may only use AI to improve review language, and editors should check with their T&F contact before using any tool.

P-INF.summary: INFORMS permits authors to use generative AI when preparing manuscripts, but AI/ML tools cannot be listed as authors and authors remain fully responsible for the accuracy and originality of the work. Any AI use must be disclosed in the acknowledgements with the tool and the nature of assistance, and references (especially AI-generated ones) must be verified against original sources. The page does not address AI use by reviewers or editors, or AI-generated images.

Reviewers may not upload any part of a manuscript to AI tools and may use AI only to polish their own written reviews, though other guidance says they must not use AI to generate review reports. Editors must not share manuscript or review information with generative AI.

AI cannot be named as an author. Submitted content must not be entered into generative AI tools because this breaches confidentiality.

P-AAA.summary: Authors may use generative AI and AI-assisted tools if they disclose the specific tools and uses and keep human oversight, taking full responsibility for the content. Disclosure goes in the methodology for research design/analysis, or in a dedicated declaration before the references for other uses; basic spelling/grammar checkers and reference managers need no disclosure. AI cannot be listed as an author, and AI creation or alteration of images is prohibited unless it is part of the research design or methods. This authors-only policy does not set rules for reviewers or editors' use of AI.

Members of the review team (reviewers and editors) must make their conclusions their own and are responsible for their accuracy. They must not upload manuscript content into generative AI tools in a way that could compromise confidentiality or copyright. No disclosure requirement, AI authorship rule, or AI image rule is stated.
